tools.name: create_planning_session
tools.title: Create Planning Session
tools.description: Create a new planning session (a scheduled production shoot) with its time slots and team members. **This is a write** — it creates real data. **REQUIRED FIELDS — CHECK THE USER'S REQUEST FIRST:** Two fields are mandatory: `productionType` (a shooting-type name/id, or the literal 'editorial') and `timeSlots` (at least one start/end). A third, `workspace`, is required ONLY when the studio is in single-client-sessions-only mode. BEFORE you do anything else, check whether the user's prompt actually gave you the required fields. If any required field is missing, DO NOT call the tool and DO NOT guess or invent a value — instead ask the user for the missing field(s) in one short message, listing all of them together (e.g. "To create this session I need: (1) the production type, (2) the date and time"). Only once you have every required field do you move on to the preview. (The tool also enforces this server-side and returns `validation_failed` listing the missing fields, but asking up-front is faster and avoids a wasted call.) **MANDATORY PREVIEW BEFORE CALLING:** Before you call this tool, you MUST first show the user a clear summary of exactly what will be created and ask them to confirm. Present it as a short table/list covering every field you're about to send — session name (or note it will be auto-named), production type, each time slot (date + start/end + timezone), location, workspace/client, producer, every team member with their skill, and any custom properties or custom resources. Then ask a direct yes/no question like "Shall I create this session?" and WAIT for the user's explicit confirmation. Only after the user says yes do you call the tool. Do NOT call the tool on the user's first request without showing this preview and getting a yes — even if every field is already known. (After you call it, the host also shows its own Allow/Deny prompt with the raw arguments; that is a second, separate gate — it does not replace your in-chat preview.) Accepts human-readable NAMES (production type, location, workspace, producer, team member people + skills) — they're resolved to IDs server-side. Pass each person as the user typed them — a name, an email, or a user id — directly into `producer`/`teamMembers`; the tool resolves it for you, so there's no need to look an id up beforehand. **This tool already verifies people and skills itself, so don't call another tool to check them first — just call it directly.** If a name is ambiguous it returns the matching candidates (with emails) for you to pick from, and if a skill is invalid it says so — so a failed call tells you exactly how to fix the arguments and retry, rather than wasting a pre-check. **Writes fail hard on unresolved names**: if a person can't be matched to exactly one user, or a skill is given that isn't a valid allowed skill the person possesses, the tool returns an error and creates nothing — it never guesses. If a name is ambiguous, pass that person's email instead. `productionType` is required (a shooting-type name/id, or the literal 'editorial'). `timeSlots` is required — a non-empty array of { start, end } ISO datetimes that each carry their own day (list multiple days for a multi-day session). A `teamMembers` skill is optional (a member can be added without one), but if you give a skill it must be a valid allowed skill the person possesses. Returns the created session (sessionId, the backend-generated `sessionCode`, name, production type, time slots, team members, workspace) so you can verify the result after it lands — after creating, the tool reads the session back so `sessionCode` reflects the real persisted value (and is the auto-name when you left `name` empty). Report the `sessionCode` to the user as the session's identifier.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Session name. Optional — if empty, the backend auto-names it (= the generated session code).

parameters.name: productionType
parameters.description: REQUIRED. Production type: a shooting-type name or id, OR the literal 'editorial' for an editorial session. Resolved to productionTypeId + contentCreationTypeId.

parameters.name: timeSlots
parameters.description: REQUIRED. Time slots as a JSON array of { start, end }, each an ISO datetime that carries its own day. A bare datetime ('2026-06-25T09:00') is wall-clock in the session timezone; add an offset/Z ('...+02:00', '...Z') only if you mean an absolute instant. **Each slot must start and end on the SAME calendar day** (in the session timezone) — a single slot CANNOT span two days, and the tool rejects one that does (e.g. 7 Jul → 8 Jul is invalid). **When the user gives a continuous range that CROSSES MIDNIGHT, you MUST SPLIT it at midnight into TWO slots — do NOT clamp the end back to the first day, and do NOT drop the after-midnight part.** Split so no requested time is lost: first slot = start → 23:59 of the start day, second slot = 00:00 of the next day → the user's end time. Example — 'from 17:00 on 7 Jul to 02:00 on 8 Jul' → [{"start":"2026-07-07T17:00","end":"2026-07-07T23:59"},{"start":"2026-07-08T00:00","end":"2026-07-08T02:00"}]. A slot needs start < end, so if the after-midnight part is zero-length (the range ends exactly at 00:00), drop the second slot and keep just [{"start":"2026-07-07T17:00","end":"2026-07-07T23:59"}]. Before sending, tell the user you've split the overnight range into two slots and confirm. **A MULTI-DAY session is likewise expressed as one slot PER DAY**: a shoot running 7–8 Jul 09:00–17:00 → TWO slots [{"start":"2026-07-07T09:00","end":"2026-07-07T17:00"},{"start":"2026-07-08T09:00","end":"2026-07-08T17:00"}], NOT one slot from 7 Jul to 8 Jul. E.g. one day, two blocks: [{"start":"2026-06-25T09:00","end":"2026-06-25T12:00"},{"start":"2026-06-25T13:00","end":"2026-06-25T17:00"}].

parameters.name: timeZone
parameters.description: Session timezone — an IANA name (e.g. 'Europe/Copenhagen', 'Asia/Tokyo'). LEAVE EMPTY to use the user's timezone (shown in the USER SETTINGS line of this tool's context) — that is the default and the common case. Only set this when the user explicitly says the shoot is in a DIFFERENT timezone. `timeSlots` are wall-clock in the resolved timezone unless a slot carries an explicit offset/Z.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Set/location name or id. Omit or 'No set' for no location.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Workspace/client name or id. Required only when the studio is in single-client-sessions-only mode.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Description. Optional, max ~2000 chars.

parameters.name: producer
parameters.description: Producer — user name (primary), or email/user id. Must resolve to exactly one user.

parameters.name: teamMembers
parameters.description: Team members as a JSON array of { person, skill }. `person` = user name (or email/id); `skill` = skill name (or id) — OPTIONAL (a member can be added without a skill). If a skill is given it must be one the person possesses that the studio allows. E.g. [{"person":"Anna Lee","skill":"Stylist"},{"person":"Bob"}].

parameters.name: customProperties
parameters.description: Custom properties as a JSON array of { name, value }. E.g. [{"name":"Campaign","value":"Spring"}]. Values are validated against the property's type: a **Number** property needs a numeric value within ±99999999999.9999; a **Free text** property is capped at 2048 characters; a **List of options** property needs one of its defined options (case-insensitive) — a bad value returns an error listing the allowed options. Dates take ISO (e.g. '2026-06-24').

parameters.name: customResources
parameters.description: Custom resources — free-form (label, person) production-support roles NOT in the standard team (e.g. catering, lunch, driver, runner, PA). JSON array of { label, name }. E.g. [{"label":"Catering","name":"John's Kitchen"},{"label":"Driver","name":"Sam"}]. Stored separately from the session core; written right after the session is created.

tools.knownLimitations: Write tool — creates a real session. `productionType` and `timeSlots` are required (no defaults). Names (production type, location, workspace, producer, crew people + skills) are resolved to IDs and FAIL HARD if unresolved — nothing is created. Custom resources are written by a second call after create; a failure there is a `warning`, not a rollback. Requires the McpWritePlanning screen (Access) + PlanningView (Write).

tools.name: delete_planning_session
tools.title: Delete Planning Session
tools.description: Delete a planning session by its id. **This is a destructive write** — it permanently removes a real session, with no pre-delete guard (mirrors the app's single 'Are you sure?' confirm). **FIND THE SESSION FIRST.** This tool only accepts a session **id** (UUID); it does NOT search. If the user refers to the session by name, code, description, date, a person on it, or any other criteria, first use the planning-session query tool to find the matching session and take its `id` — do not guess an id. If that lookup returns more than one match, ask the user which one before deleting. **MANDATORY PREVIEW BEFORE CALLING:** before you call this tool, show the user exactly which session will be deleted — its name and code (and date/time if helpful, from the lookup result) — and ask a direct yes/no like "Delete this session?". Only call the tool after the user confirms. Do NOT delete on the user's first request without this preview and an explicit yes. (After you call it, the host also shows its own Allow/Deny prompt; that is a second, separate gate — it does not replace your in-chat preview.) Returns { deleted: true, sessionId } on success.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: REQUIRED. The session id (UUID) to delete — obtained from a prior planning-session query's `id` field. This tool does not resolve names or codes; pass a UUID.

tools.knownLimitations: Destructive write — permanently removes a session, with no pre-delete guard (mirrors the app's single confirm). Takes a session id (UUID) ONLY; it does not search — find the session with query_planning first, then pass its id. Single id only (bulk delete is out of scope). Requires McpWritePlanning (Access) + PlanningView (Write).

tools.name: get_asset_preview
tools.title: Get Asset Preview
tools.description: Get inline image previews for digital assets so the user can see them. Use when the user wants to SEE / VIEW / DISPLAY / RENDER specific assets or images. Accepts a list of asset IDs — typically obtained from query_asset (or any other tool that returns asset IDs). Returns a JSON object with a `previews` array of { id, url, fileName }. **The images are rendered for the user by the paired preview widget — do NOT also embed them in your reply.** Specifically: do NOT output any Markdown image tags (`![...](url)`) or the preview URLs in your text; the widget already shows every image, so repeating them produces duplicate 'Show Image' blocks. Just answer in words (e.g. how many, which ones, filenames) and let the widget display the pictures. URLs are short-lived presigned links. Do NOT use for searching, listing, or counting assets — use query_asset for that. Prefer assetIds — use fileIds only when you have no assetId for the image. If both are given, assetIds is used and fileIds is ignored.

parameters.name: assetIds
parameters.description: Asset IDs to fetch preview images for. Pass as a JSON array of strings, e.g. ["id1","id2"]. Get IDs from query_asset or any tool that returns assetIds.

parameters.name: fileIds
parameters.description: File IDs (a `fileId` from any tool that returns one) — a different id space from assetIds. Use when a tool gives you a fileId rather than an assetId. Ignored when assetIds is set.

tools.knownLimitations: Hard cap of 200 IDs per call (extras are dropped and `truncated: true` is returned). Preview URLs are short-lived presigned links that expire. Returns images only — use query_asset to search/list/count. `assetIds` is the primary input; `fileIds` is a narrow editorial-only side path for editorial-document / brief mood-board / mock-up images (from query_editorial_detail / query_deliverable_detail). The two are DIFFERENT id spaces and are never mixed — if both are passed, assetIds wins and fileIds is ignored (a `note` says so). `previews[].id` is the assetId (assetIds path) or the fileId (fileIds path).

tools.name: get_styleguide_detail
tools.title: Get Style Guide Detail
tools.description: Get the full content of a single style guide by id or by name, organized the way the Style Guide screen is (a General section + one entry per production type, split into tabs). Pass 'styleGuideId' (GUID, e.g. from query_styleguide) OR 'name' (resolved to an id via search; exact match preferred, ambiguous names return candidates). Returns a header (name, internalName, workspace, isEnabled/isInvalid, versionNumber, settingType, hasNewerVersion, created/updated, deepLinkUrl), a 'general' block { description, coverImage (image metadata only), colorMatching (color-reference rules, only when enabled — incl. colorAccurateStep for approach 'Use Selection from Production Type' and perProductionTypeAccurateSteps for the first-production-type approach), categoryTriggers (assigned product-category names), other (nonSelectAssetsOutputName), properties (style-guide custom props as [{name,value}]) }, and 'productionTypes': [{ name, workflow (the workflow this type's work runs through — its name; use it to chain into get_workflow_detail), kind ('visual' or 'text'), isEnabled, description (production-type-level brief), referenceImages (PT-level reference files, metadata only), variantMapping, heroPosition (name of the hero position), and tabs }]. Each tab is OMITTED when it has no data, so a type only shows the tabs it actually configures. Tab visibility also MIRRORS the Style Guide screen: a tab is only returned when the production type's assigned workflow actually contains the matching step — Capture needs a capture step, External/Internal Post their post steps, Copywriting/Localization a copywriting step, Delivery an asset-delivery step wired to a connection the workspace owns (Delivery additionally requires the Advanced Style Guides plan feature or pre-existing saved routing; Localization the Localization plan feature). So a tab the user cannot see on the screen is not surfaced here. (This step-based gating is only applied when the assigned workflow is resolvable; if it isn't, tabs fall back to being shown whenever they carry data.) Visual types use: 'capture' { assignedWorkflow (the bound workflow name), description, condition (the PRODUCTION-TYPE-level condition — when this whole production type is active; it gates every position beneath it), files (PT reference files, image metadata only), positions: [{ name, isHero, isOptional, isPhotoReview, type, mediaType, isColorReference, isEnforceAlts, minShotsAlts, shots { minShots, maxShots }, description, exampleImages (position cover) / referenceImages (position attachments) (image METADATA only — fileName, size, mediaType, previewUrl; never the binary; a bare { fileId } is returned when the asset service has no metadata for it), condition (decoded position rules — see _fieldNotes.condition/ruleType), properties (position custom props) }] }, 'presetsAndNaming' { positions: [{ position, preset (the selected preset name), presetId (the preset's id — chain it into query_preset_detail to explain the preset's full config; this is how 'what preset is applied to job/style guide X' is answered), namePattern (output naming), specs: [{ variantNumber, variantCode, isEnabled, namePattern, spec (the variant's real spec — dimensions/format/dpi/color-space/crop/… ) }] }] }, 'internalPost' { retouchingBrief { description, files, goodExamples, badExamples }, videoBrief { description, files } } (per production type; image metadata only), 'trigger' { type (when this production type's work is triggered — e.g. 'On product creation' or 'When a step of a specific production type is done'), sources: [{ sourceProductionType, steps, passThroughAssets, positionsToPassThrough (the generative 'Positions to Pass Through' — [{ position, tag }]) }] }, 'externalPost' { steps (per-step external-post flags), positions: [{ position, mappings: [{ step, flow, vendor, folderPattern (FTP), pixelzTemplate / pixelzFallbackTemplate / gatewayTemplate / brightRiverTemplate (the main template), variantTemplates: [{ variant (variantCode), template, fallbackTemplate }] (the per-variant template-of-variants mapping) }] }] }, 'delivery' { connections (the delivery connections the assigned workflow delivers to — the matrix columns, when resolvable), rows: [{ position, variant (which output — 'main' or 'variant N'; absent for a whole-position row), deliveredToAll (true = delivered to every connection), deliveredConnections, excludedConnections }] }, and 'properties' (production-type custom props). When DESCRIBING delivery, summarize exception-style, NOT row-by-row: name the connection(s), then — since most outputs are delivered everywhere — state the default (e.g. 'all N outputs delivered to all connections') and list ONLY the outputs that deviate (an output with excludedConnections, or a partial deliveredConnections). Never enumerate every output when they are all deliveredToAll. If 'connections' is absent, say the specific connection list isn't available (the production type has no resolvable assigned workflow) and describe delivery by deliveredToAll/excludedConnections only. Text/copywriting types use: 'copywriting' { configuration (config name), layouts (the configuration's layout/screen NAMES in display order — the copywriter's data-entry form is split into these named screens), fields (the configured fields, ordered — each has { name, type (Single Line Text / Text Area / Care Instructions / Color / Hidden Field / Predefined List / Material Composition / Custom Content Widget), layout ({ name (which layout/screen the field sits on — matches an entry in `layouts`), row, column (its place on the 12-column grid; row top→bottom, column left→right); ABSENT when the field is not placed on any layout), deliveryName (the API delivery key), required (the configuration default 'Required'/'Optional'), minLength, maxLength (character/selection limits), autoTranslation (text fields), conditionalDelivery (hidden fields) } plus the type-specific settings that apply: Text Area → richText, deliveryFormat (HTML/Markdown), textFormat (enabled rich-text toggles); Predefined List → displayType (Dropdown/Multiple choice selection/Tagging), options (the choice names); Color → colors [{ name, value (hex) }]; Care Instructions → symbols [{ category, variations (enabled symbol names) }]; Material Composition → materialComposition { components, materials, disclaimers }; Single Line/Text Area/Hidden → prefill (the rendered data-merge default). Text fields may also carry guidelines { preferredWords, forbiddenWords, neverUseEmojis, conventions[{ term, correct, dontWrite }] } and Text Area may carry ai { enabled, instruction, referenceExample }. Any field may carry condition (decoded conditional-visibility rules). Only the blocks that apply to the field's type / that are configured are present), fieldSettings (per-field overrides — visibility/required/conditionalDelivery/skipTranslation — only fields that differ from the configuration default) }, 'localization' { locale, bundleByStyle }, 'presetsAndNaming' { fileOutputName }, 'delivery' { connections, rows: [{ field, deliveredToAll, deliveredConnections, excludedConnections }] } (a per-field × delivery-connection matrix — same shape as visual delivery), 'trigger' { type, sourceProductionTypes, conjunction, step }, and 'properties' (text PT custom props). When DESCRIBING a copywriting production type, GROUP the fields by their layout: present one section per name in `layouts` (in that order), listing the fields whose `layout.name` matches — ordered by layout.row then layout.column (the on-screen reading order). Put any field with no `layout` in a final 'Not placed on a layout' section. This mirrors how the copywriter actually sees the form. Pass 'productType' (a production type name e.g. 'On-Model', or a numeric shootingTypeId) to narrow the result to just that production type. **Use cases**: (1) Explain what a style guide covers — which production types it defines and, per type, the capture brief, naming, trigger rules, or copywriting config. (2) Inspect a type's positions (hero / optional / photo-review), shot rules, and reference/example images. (3) Read the description / styling rules, the asset naming, or the copywriting field configuration. By default the latest published version is returned; pass 'includeDraft=true' to prefer the draft, or 'versionId' to fetch a specific version. Pass 'raw=true' to also return the untouched styleGuide object (copywriting, properties, positions detail) for deep inspection. By default the response is human-readable: each production type shows its resolved 'name' (not the numeric shootingTypeId) and raw ids (record id, version ids) are omitted. Pass 'includeIds=true' ONLY when the user explicitly asks for raw ids/version ids (record id, versionId, latestVersionId, draftVersionId, numeric shootingTypeId, per-type workflowDefinitionId/workflowDefinitionVersionId, positionId, preset specId, image fileId). The visual widget (production-type accordion with reference images) is OPT-IN via 'showWidget=true' (default false) — set it ONLY when the user explicitly asks to SEE the style guide visually (show the style guide / its reference images/photos / visualize). By default the full content (incl. all conditions/rules the accordion does not render) is returned as plain data and no widget is drawn.

parameters.name: styleGuideId
parameters.description: Style guide id (GUID) to fetch, e.g. from query_styleguide. Provide this OR 'name'. A non-GUID value passed here is treated as a name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Style guide name to look up instead of an id. Exact (case-insensitive) match preferred; partial search otherwise. Provide this OR 'styleGuideId'.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Workspace/client name or ID to disambiguate when resolving by name. Optional.

parameters.name: includeDraft
parameters.description: Prefer the draft version over the latest published. Default false.

parameters.name: versionId
parameters.description: Fetch a specific style guide version id. Omit to resolve via the style guide's overview.

parameters.name: raw
parameters.description: Return the full untouched styleGuide object as well. Default false (curated summary only).

parameters.name: productType
parameters.description: Narrow the result to a single production type (shooting type) — pass its name (e.g. 'On-Model') or numeric shootingTypeId. Omit to return all production types. Only the matching productionTypes[] entry is returned; the header is unchanged.

parameters.name: includeIds
parameters.description: Include raw ids (record id, versionId, latestVersionId, draftVersionId, numeric shootingTypeId, positionId, image fileId, preset specId) and numeric type/mediaTypeId. Default false — human-readable names only. Set true only when the user explicitly asks for ids.

parameters.name: showWidget
parameters.description: Render the style guide as a visual widget (production-type accordion with reference images). Default false. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to SEE the style guide visually — e.g. 'show me the style guide', 'show the reference images/photos', 'visualize'. When false the full content is returned as plain data (incl. all conditions/rules) and no widget is drawn.

tools.exampleOutput: { "name": "Spring 2026 Apparel", "workspace": "Acme", "settingType": "Published", "general": { "description": "...", "colorMatching": { "required": true, "approach": "Use Selection from Production Type", "colorAccurateStep": "Photography" }, "other": { "nonSelectAssetsOutputName": "_non-select-%product_code" }, "categoryTriggers": ["Dresses"] }, "productionTypes": [ { "name": "On-Model", "workflow": "Apparel Std", "kind": "visual", "capture": { "assignedWorkflow": "Apparel Std", "description": "...", "condition": [ { "rules": [ { "ruleType": "Property Rule", "detail": { "property": "Job Code", "operator": "Contains", "value": "Flat" } } ] } ], "positions": [ { "name": "Front", "isHero": true, "shots": { "minShots": 1, "maxShots": 3 }, "condition": [ { "rules": [ { "ruleType": "Production Rule", "detail": { "outfit": "Producing an outfit" } }, { "ruleType": "Source Rule", "detail": { "source": "Source is VENDOR PROVIDED" } } ] } ] } ] }, "presetsAndNaming": { "positions": [ { "position": "Front", "preset": "Web Std", "specs": [ { "variantCode": "M", "spec": { "width": 2000 } } ] } ] }, "internalPost": { "retouchingBrief": { "description": "..." } } } ], "_fieldNotes": { "condition": "OR'd sections; rules within a section are AND'd", "ruleType": "Property / Production (outfit) / Source / Sub Function Output / Instruction Rule" } }
tools.knownLimitations: Fetch ONE style guide by id or name (use query_styleguide to find the id); resolves the latest published version by default (includeDraft=true for the draft). Names are human-readable — pass includeIds=true for raw ids, raw=true for the untouched payload. The visual widget is opt-in via showWidget=true (default false — full content incl. conditions is returned as plain data); set it only when the user asks to SEE the style guide. A per-PT tab is omitted when it has no data. Visual PTs surface capture (assignedWorkflow/description/PT-level condition/files/positions), presetsAndNaming (preset + per-variant spec detail), externalPost (incl. per-variant template mappings), internalPost, delivery, properties; text PTs surface copywriting, localization, presetsAndNaming (fileOutputName), delivery matrix, trigger, properties; generative trigger surfaces passThroughAssets + positionsToPassThrough. Conditions are decoded at two levels — position (capture.positions[].condition) and production type (capture.condition, gates all positions) — each as OR'd sections of AND'd rules; ruleType is one of Property / Production (outfit) / Source / Sub Function Output / Instruction, and a Property rule's operator label depends on the property's data type (Date/Number/Text) — see _fieldNotes. Variant-level conditions live on the preset, surfaced by query_preset (not duplicated here). Filtering to a productType that does not exist in the studio returns a productTypeWarning (distinct from a real-but-unconfigured type). Positions, copywriting config, presets, and asset metadata are best-effort enrichments (may be absent on backend failure). Asset images are metadata-only (fileName/size/previewUrl) — never the binary; a bare { fileId } is returned when metadata can't be resolved. The Delivery matrix is returned as text/JSON only (the widget does not render it); per-PT workflow (and the delivery connection columns derived from it) resolves via the workflow binding carried on the PTSG payload — absent only when the PT truly has no assigned workflow. The widget shows the assigned workflow, the Internal Post briefs (incl. good/bad example galleries), and a visible file name on every file.

tools.name: get_talent_crew_preview
tools.title: Get Talent & Crew Preview
tools.description: Inline avatar GALLERY widget for a list of talent crew IDs. **TRIGGER STRICTLY when user prompt is purely visual** — e.g. 'show me their faces', 'what do they look like', 'photo gallery of these models'. **DO NOT TRIGGER**:   • after `query_talent_crew` (its table widget already shows Photo column)   • after `query_talent_crew_schedule` (its widget renders avatars inline post-improvements-v1)   • for 'show profile' / 'who is X' / 'list talents' (use `query_talent_crew`) **Best fit**: standalone visual question without data context. Returns `previews` array of { talentCrewId, displayName, avatarUrl, deepLinkUrl }. Widget owns visual — text response = ONE sentence ('Showing N avatars.').

parameters.name: talentCrewIds
parameters.description: Talent crew IDs to fetch avatar previews for. Pass as a JSON array of strings, e.g. ["id1","id2"].

tools.knownLimitations: Visual-only avatar gallery. Do NOT chain after query_talent_crew or query_talent_crew_schedule — those already render avatars. Avatars are resolved in chunks of 50; talent without an avatarId are omitted.

tools.name: get_text_asset_content
tools.title: Get Text Asset Content
tools.description: Read the submitted COPY (body text) of one or more copywriting (Text) assets — the configured fields (Title, Description, Care instructions, Material composition, Colour, Predefined lists), grouped by layout, with every selection field's internal ids resolved to their configured names, plus Colour swatches and Care-symbol images, and each task's language. This is the DETAIL companion to query_asset / query_task: find text assets first (a query_asset hit with isTextAsset:true, or a query_task hit) and pass their taskId(s) here. Use when the user wants to SEE / COMPARE / SUMMARISE the actual copy for a product (e.g. 'show me the German copy', 'compare the EN and DE description', 'what does this product's copy say'). Pass ONE taskId to open a single task, or SEVERAL to compare languages side by side (e.g. the EN + DE tasks of the same product). Only taskIds are needed — the work unit, product and language are resolved from Elasticsearch. Returns submitted content only (not unsaved drafts); an empty field returns an empty value (never an error). BUNDLE tasks: a style-bundle work unit has several products that each have their OWN copy for the same task, so one such taskId returns MULTIPLE items (one per product, isBundle:true, same taskId/workUnitId) — treat them as one bundle and present/switch by productCode (mirrors the Gamma product picker). A taskId that isn't found, or whose work unit isn't a Text asset, is reported under notFound / notCopywriting rather than failing the whole call.

parameters.name: taskIds
parameters.description: The copywriting task id(s) to open. Pass a single GUID string, or a JSON array of GUID strings to open several tasks at once (e.g. the EN and DE tasks of one product to compare). Get them from a query_asset text-asset hit (isTextAsset:true) or a query_task hit. No name resolution.

parameters.name: showPreview
parameters.description: Render the copy as a visual preview widget (cards with swatches / care-symbol images). Default true — this tool exists to preview copy, so normally leave it on. Set false ONLY when you are chaining this call to extract the copy as plain data (e.g. to summarise or compare in text) and do NOT want the widget to pop up — the copy is still returned as JSON either way.

tools.name: get_workflow_detail

tools.description: Get the full definition of a single workflow (production pipeline template) by id or by name. Pass 'workflowId' (GUID, e.g. from query_workflow) OR 'name' (resolved to an id via search; exact match preferred, ambiguous names return candidates). tools.name: query_collection
tools.title: Query Collection
tools.description: Search collections — Creative Force's mechanism for sharing assets out to EXTERNAL reviewers for feedback, approval, and decisions (external review collaboration). A collection groups assets (from jobs/products or editorial deliverables) so invited external reviewers can approve, comment, and make decisions. OPTIONAL param `collectionType` picks which kind of collection to search: 'Photo Review' (2) and 'Post Review' (1) — the two review types shown together on the merged Review Collections screen; 'Review' — a convenience value = Photo Review + Post Review together (the merged screen); 'Selection' (6, collaborative final-asset selection); 'Gallery' (7, published gallery). **If `collectionType` is omitted it DEFAULTS to 'Review'** (Photo + Post Review) — the response then carries `isDefaultCollectionType:true` and a `hint`; surface that hint to the user (e.g. 'Showing Review collections by default — say Selection/Gallery/Photo Review/Post Review to narrow'). When the user names a type explicitly, no hint is returned. **IMPORTANT — Short List collections are NOT handled by this tool.** A Short List (Talent & Crew) is a distinct collection type (functionType 5); this tool cannot search it and 'Short List' is NOT a valid `collectionType` here. If the user asks about short lists (e.g. 'show my short lists', 'short lists containing model X', 'talent short lists awaiting feedback'), use the separate **query_shortlist** tool instead — do NOT call query_collection for that. All identifiers are names/codes — resolved to IDs automatically. Draft and Backlog collections are hidden (not filterable). When any groupBy* param is set, returns aggregation buckets instead of a list; pageSize=0 returns count only. Each collection type requires its subscription add-on; querying a type the studio hasn't purchased returns an explanatory error, not an empty list. FILTER SCOPE BY TYPE — each type exposes a DIFFERENT filter set (see each param's 'APPLIES TO'); do NOT pass a filter outside its type or you'll get empty/misleading results:   • Review / Photo Review / Post Review (can be E-comm or Editorial — use contentType to narrow): name, owner, workspace, status, state, decisionMade, comments, invitationSent, collectionRound, contentType, job*, product*, project*, deliverable*, roundOfReview.   • Selection: name, owner, workspace, status, state, decisionMade, comments, invitationSent, project*, deliverable*. NO job/product, collectionRound, contentType, roundOfReview.   • Gallery: name, owner, workspace, state, comments, invitationSent, project*. NO status, decisionMade, deliverable, job/product, collectionRound, contentType, roundOfReview.   (invitationSent = invitationSentFrom/To, applies to all three since any of them can be shared.) TEXT FILTERS — this param accepts inline operators (collectionName): Plain text = exact match (case-insensitive). Supports inline operators (case-insensitive): 'isNotEmpty' (has any value), 'isEmpty' (no value), 'contains:foo', 'notContains:foo', 'ne:foo' (not equal), 'eq:foo' (exact). E.g. to find records where this field has a value, pass 'isNotEmpty'. (Job/Product/Project/Deliverable code+name are exact-match option filters, not inline-operator text.)

tools.description: Search Editorial Productions (also called Editorial work units) — the central WorkUnit-doc row that tracks an Editorial Deliverable's content through the workflow (contentCreationTypeId=2). For any 'per workspace' or 'per client' breakdown, use groupByWorkspace=true — do not try to derive workspace names from list results. Editorial only — for E-comm production rows use query_ecomm_production. For the parent project itself use query_editorial_project; for deliverable-level filtering use query_editorial_deliverable.

Mirrors the Event Log panel in the CF web app (Gamma): an audit trail of an item's past activities and changes. This tool is ALWAYS scoped to a single item: you MUST identify the entity first (there is no workspace-wide event search). Use it to answer: 'what changed on product X recently?', 'show check-in/out history for sample Y', 'who updated this product and when?', 'history of this workflow / style guide / editorial project / deliverable'. entityType is required ('product', 'sample', 'workflow', 'styleguide', 'editorialProject' or 'editorialDeliverable'). For product, pass the product code as `entity`. For sample, pass the sample's GUID (id) as `entity` plus the product code. For workflow, styleguide, editorialProject and editorialDeliverable, pass the entity's GUID (id) as `entity`. Filters (all optional): event type name(s), user, date range, free-text keyword, and — product only — step and job code; sample only — location. DATE WINDOW: there are THREE cases. (1) User gives no time frame → leave lastMonths, dateFrom and dateTo ALL empty; the tool applies the same default Gamma uses ('Last 3 months'). (2) User asks for the last N months ('last 4 months', 'past 6 months') → pass `lastMonths`=N and leave dateFrom/dateTo empty; the tool computes it EXACTLY as Gamma's 'Last N months' filter. (3) User names an ABSOLUTE period with concrete dates/months ('in May', 'since 2026-05-01') → pass dateFrom/dateTo. CRITICAL: never hand-compute a 'last N months' range into dateFrom/dateTo (e.g. 'today minus N months' / 'the last 90 days') — Gamma's calculation is calendar-aligned with an N-1 offset in the user's timezone, so a naive subtraction will NOT match the app. Only lastMonths (or the empty default) matches. The exact range actually searched is returned as `dateWindowSearched` (already in the user's timezone) — cite THAT when telling the user which period you checked, and do not recompute it. If the user truly wants the item's entire history, pass entityCreatedDate (the item's creation date) instead of a wide dateFrom — that is the safe, bounded way to cover full history. IMPORTANT: when the default 3-month window is used and 0 events come back, that does NOT mean the item has no history — older events are simply outside the window. The response says so (dateWindowNote); in that case, re-query with entityCreatedDate (or an explicit range) and tell the user you initially only checked the last 3 months. EVENT TYPE: pass human-readable event name(s) (e.g. 'Checked-in', 'Properties updated'); they are resolved to the catalog. Omit to return all events. Each record has: dateTime (ISO), user (may be empty for automated/system events), event, eventGroup, and a free-text `details` description (there is no structured before/after state). Results are newest-first; supports paging (page/pageSize). NOTE: there are no events before October 2022. Treat this only as the earliest possible data — do NOT use it as a dateFrom to fetch all history (use entityCreatedDate for that).

The Event Log scan for a product is anchored on this date; without it the query is unreliable (may time out or miss events), so never call query_event_log for a product before you have its created date. For the other entity types, providing it (chained from the entity's query tool `created`) is recommended and improves reliability on items with long histories; safe to omit (the tool falls back to the default 3-month window).

parameters.description: Event type filter — THE correct way to limit results to specific kinds of events (the named actions in the log). ALWAYS use this param when the user asks for a specific kind of event ('check-in/out events', 'status changes', 'reset', 'property updates', 'location changes'); do NOT put the event-type name in `keyword`. Just pass the term(s) as the user phrased them — you do NOT need the exact catalog name. The tool matches GENEROUSLY: each term you pass matches every catalog event whose name contains it (e.g. 'status change' covers all *Status Change events; 'reset' covers Product Reset and Work Unit Reset). The response tells you EXACTLY which event types were searched (`eventTypesCovered`) and lists any term that matched nothing (`eventTypeSuggestions`) so you can re-query. Because the tool reports its coverage back to you, TRUST this filter: do NOT fetch all events and filter them yourself, and do NOT skip the filter for fear of a wrong name. Just report to the user which event types were covered. Omit only when the user genuinely wants ALL event types. Pass a JSON array of names.

Pass just the integer N. The tool then computes the window EXACTLY as the CF web app (Gamma) does for its 'Last N months' filter (a calendar-aligned window in the user's timezone). Do NOT try to reproduce that yourself with dateFrom/dateTo (e.g. 'today minus N months') — Gamma's calculation is not a naive N-month subtraction, so a hand-computed range will NOT match the app. Omit when the user gives no time frame (the tool defaults to the same as lastMonths=3) or when the user names an ABSOLUTE range (then use dateFrom/dateTo).

parameters.name: dateFrom

Leave empty otherwise — do not invent a wide start date to 'see everything' (that risks timeouts); the tool defaults to the last 3 months. For full history, use entityCreatedDate instead.

parameters.description: Max results per page. Default 50.

tools.name: query_planning
tools.title: Query Planning
tools.description: **Custom Resource trigger** → if user prompt names a production support role NOT in the standard productionTeam (Photographer/Stylist/Model/Art Director/Hair&Makeup/Assistant/Videographer/DigitalProcessing) → call this tool with `includeCustomResources=true`. Common triggers: 'cater', 'lunch', 'runner', 'driver', 'PA', 'DIT', 'dog handler', 'medic' (and any similar free-form role). Custom Resource labels are FREE-FORM text studios type themselves → semantic-match them yourself from `customResourceLabelsAvailable[]` + `customResources[]` in the response. **Tool-first, ask-later**: call the tool, then if `customResourceLabelsAvailable=[]` ask user; otherwise semantic-match from availableLabels. **Trailing-junk / cut-off tolerance**: if user prompt has trailing backslash (`\`), ellipsis (`...`), question marks (`??`), or appears truncated mid-word, IGNORE the noise and treat the readable trigger word as the query. Do NOT respond with 'your message looks cut off' — call the tool with the cleaned query. Examples: 'Who is today's Cater' → query for cater. 'Lunch...' → query for lunch. 'DIT??' → query for DIT. **Likely-misread tolerance**: if a trigger word could be misread as a proper noun (e.g. 'Cater' → 'Carter', 'DIT' → a person's initials), DEFAULT to the production-role interpretation (this tool is in a production planning context, not a general-knowledge chat). Don't suggest sports/celebrity readings of trigger words. **Default 'today' to ISO date**: when user says 'today', 'hôm nay', 'this morning', etc., automatically set `dateFrom`=`dateTo`=current date in `YYYY-MM-DD`, computed in the USER's timezone (see `_userSettings` in prior tool results) — NOT UTC. Same for 'tomorrow' (+1 day), 'yesterday' (-1 day), 'this week' (Mon-Sun current week). Pass date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` values: the server interprets each date's day boundaries in the user's timezone, so no manual UTC offset is needed. Don't ask the user to specify the date when they used a relative phrase. Search planning sessions — scheduled production shoots with team, time slots, and progress. Use this to answer: what's planned, when (ISO 8601 UTC), where, who's on set, sample check-in status, photography progress, alerts. **Who-is-working queries**: when user asks 'who is working this week', 'which talent has sessions today', 'list photographers on sessions next month' → set `groupByTeamMember=true` with `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Response flips to person-centric: each entry shows the team member with their sessions. This is the primary way to answer talent-on-session questions when the studio does not use the Resource Booking add-on. Filter by team member (any role) or specific role (photographer, stylist, model, art director, assistant, videographer, hair & makeup). Also filter by sessionCode (e.g. 'SES137123CF'), sessionName (partial), sessionDescription (exact), location, production type, check-in/alert/photography status, date range. Supports custom property filters via customPropertyFilters (JSON array of {name, value} for exact match or {name, from, to} for a Date range. Number-type properties also support a comparison operator (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/between/notBetween) mirroring the UI — see the customPropertyFilters param for the exact shape). CUSTOM PROPERTIES: each session's `customProperties` lists only properties that have a value SET. A property name being absent from a session does NOT mean it is undefined — it may be defined-but-unset. Before telling the user a custom property does not exist (or is missing) for sessions, call query_property(entityType='session') to get the full list of properties defined for this studio; never conclude a property is undefined from a query_planning result alone. Filter by associated job (jobCode/jobName, or `job` ambiguous = code OR name) and product attributes (productCode/productName, or `product` ambiguous = code OR name, plus brand, category, color, styleCode) — exact match, case-insensitive, matches if ANY of the session's jobs/products satisfies the filter. Editorial workflow: filter by associated project (projectCode/projectName, or `project` ambiguous = code OR name, plus campaign) and deliverable (deliverableCode/deliverableName, or `deliverable` ambiguous = code OR name, plus deliverableOutputName) — exact match, case-insensitive, matches if ANY of the session's projects/deliverables satisfies the filter. Use `user` to find a session where a given user is on the production team regardless of skill/role (V2 ProductionTeams). Returns: session `id` (UUID), sessionName, sessionCode, time slots (ISO 8601 UTC), full production team (resolved names), check-in status, photography progress, job codes, product codes. When groupBy params set, returns counts/aggregations instead of list. **Session lookup param choice — strict per user phrasing:**   • User says 'session code SES137123CF' / 'code SES…' → `sessionCode` only.   • User says 'session named Nike Spring' / 'the Spring shoot' → `sessionName` only.   • User says 'session SES137123CF' / 'session Nike Spring' WITHOUT specifying code-vs-name → `session` (ambiguous param, matches code OR name OR UUID). Don't pass multiple session params at once — pick the one that matches user intent. **Chain with query_talent_crew_schedule**: when the user asks about bookings/holds for a specific session, FIRST call this tool → take response's `id` and `timeSlots` → pass to `query_talent_crew_schedule(sessionId=<id>, dateFrom=<min start>, dateTo=<max end>, ...)`. **Custom Resource queries** (cater / catering / lunch / food / runner / driver / transport / PA / production assistant / makeup artist (one-off) / any role NOT in standard productionTeam): set `includeCustomResources=true`. Custom resources are free-form (label, name) pairs attached inline to a session via the FE 'CUSTOM RESOURCE' panel → free-form means studios type whatever they want ('cater', 'Cater', 'catering', 'lunch', 'food service'). The tool returns ALL custom resources on the page and Claude does the semantic match (no server-side filter — too many false-negatives on free-form text like 'Caster' vs 'cater'). **Semantic match rule** (CRITICAL for custom resources): the response includes `customResourceLabelsAvailable: string[]` → distinct labels seen on the page, plus `customResources[{label,name}]` per session. Scan `customResourceLabelsAvailable` for labels **semantically similar** to the user's word, then read the matching `customResources` entries. DO NOT reply 'not found' until you've checked every label. Examples: 'cater' → look for 'catering', 'lunch', 'meal', 'food service', 'snack runner'; 'driver' → 'transport', 'shuttle', 'logistics'; 'PA' → 'production assistant', 'runner', 'gopher'. Tell the user which labels you considered (e.g. 'No exact 'cater' label, but 'catering' is set to John Smith → likely the same role.'). **Custom resource has NO booking status** (no Confirmed/Hold) → it's session-inline data, not a resource booking. Don't mention status pills for these rows. TEXT FILTERS — these params accept inline operators (sessionDescription): Plain text = exact match (case-insensitive). Supports inline operators (case-insensitive): 'isNotEmpty' (has any value), 'isEmpty' (no value), 'contains:foo', 'notContains:foo', 'ne:foo' (not equal), 'eq:foo' (exact). E.g. to find records where this field has a value, pass 'isNotEmpty'.

tools.description: Open ONE preset (E-comm or Editorial, Photo or Video) by id and return its full, fully-typed output spec configuration — every output variant and nested auto-variant, with every enum id resolved to the name the Studio-Settings preset popup shows. This is the DETAIL companion to query_presets (the LIST tool): query_presets finds a preset by name/workspace/media type; this tool drills into one. It is id-only — it does NOT resolve names. When the user names a preset, call query_presets(keyword=…) first and chain the returned 'id' (and 'presetType'). (Field meanings for interpreting the response — variantCount, specs[], autoVariants, colorProfile, video codec/frameRate, editorial namingConvention, metadataRules, etc. — are in the response '_fieldNotes'; read them there, not here.) Each spec carries a 'specLabel' ('Main' / 'Spec-1' / 'Spec-2'… — or 'Spec' when the preset has only one) that mirrors the name shown in the Studio-Settings preset popup sidebar; ALWAYS refer to a spec by its specLabel when answering the user (that's what they see on screen), not by variantCode. tools.name: query_talent_crew

tools.description: Search talent and resource users — both license users (internal team members) and resource users (freelancers, models, agencies). Use this to answer: who is on the team, who has a given skill, what agency a model belongs to, counts of talent by skill / employment type / status. User types: License (internal), Resource (external). Employment types: Permanent, Freelance. States: Enabled, Disabled, NotVerify, Deleted. Common skills: Photographer, Stylist, Model, Art Director, Hair & Makeup, Retoucher, Videographer, Producer, Assistant, Project Manager, Deliverable Owner, Digital Processing. Filter by name, job title, user type, employment type, skill, state, agency, short list, contact info, city, created date range. Supports custom property filters via customPropertyFilters (JSON array of {name, value} for exact match or {name, from, to} for a Date range. Number-type properties also support a comparison operator (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/between/notBetween) mirroring the UI — see the customPropertyFilters param for the exact shape). CUSTOM PROPERTIES: each record's `customProperties` lists only properties that have a value SET. A property name being absent from a record does NOT mean it is undefined — it may be defined-but-unset. Before telling the user a custom property does not exist (or is missing) for talent/crew, call query_property(entityType='talent_crew') to get the full list of properties defined for this studio; never conclude a property is undefined from a query_talent_crew result alone. Pass `talentCrewIds` (JSON array of talent crew IDs from query_talent_crew_schedule or other tools) to look up specific records directly instead of re-querying by skill. Use human-readable names for all filters (resolved to IDs automatically). Each record includes a `deepLinkUrl` to the talent detail page in the web app. Each record also carries a `collections` array — the review collections and short lists the talent belongs to ({ collectionId, collectionName, status, round, hasComment }). To inspect those collections, chain the `collectionId`s into query_collection(collectionIds=[...]). **CRITICAL — UI rendering ownership**: an inline widget handles record-list and aggregation responses, so your text must NOT duplicate them. Per response shape:   • `hits` with ≥1 talent → widget renders compact-card / table. Text = ONE brief sentence (e.g. 'Found 6 talents in the Christmas 24 short list.').   • Aggregation (`byAgency` / `bySkill` / `byStatus` / `byUserType` / `byEmploymentType`) → widget renders bar-chart sections. Text = ONE brief sentence summarising top buckets (e.g. '15 agencies, top 3: ACME (12), aaa (9), 234234 (8).').   • `hits` empty + `total > 0` (count-only, pageSize=0) → widget HIDES (0 height). Text MUST state the count plainly (e.g. 'Có **123** photographers đang active.').   • `hits` empty + `total = 0` → widget HIDES. Text = brief negative reply (e.g. 'Không có crew member nào match.'). Do NOT write a markdown table, list, gallery, or any field-by-field summary. Do NOT embed `![image](avatarUrl)` or `[Show Image](url)`. Do NOT include deep-link URLs in text — the widget already renders the name as a clickable anchor. Avatars are shown by default in compact-card and table views. Pass `includeAvatar=false` only when the caller explicitly wants to skip avatar resolution (e.g. perf-sensitive bulk queries). Still no markdown images in your text — the widget owns the visual. **"Talent" terminology** — `skill="Talent"` is a PSEUDO-SKILL meaning Models + AI Models only (server-side OR-match). ✅ TRIGGER on standalone words: "talent", "talents", "a talent", "the talents", "find a talent", "show me talents", "model agency", or context implying Models specifically. Examples: 'Find a talent named Jane' → { name: 'Jane', skill: 'Talent' }; 'How many talents do we have?' → { skill: 'Talent', pageSize: 0 }. ❌ DO NOT TRIGGER on: 'Talent & Crew' / 'Talent and Crew' / 'talents and crew' — these are the FULL ENTITY NAME (License + Resource = whole pool). They contain the word "Talent" but mean the OPPOSITE — search broad pool, omit `skill`. Examples: 'Find Talent & Crew named Han' → { name: 'Han' } NO skill; 'How many Talent & Crew based in London' → { city: 'London' } NO skill. ❌ DO NOT TRIGGER for explicit roles (Photographers, Stylists, Producers, Hair & Makeup, Videographers, internal team) — pass the explicit skill name or omit the filter. When groupBy params are set, returns counts / aggregations instead of a list. Each hit includes a `rates` array (rateId, name, amount, currency, duration, rateType, agencyFee, payrollFee, isDefault, description) **only if the caller has the `Rates` screen permission**. Top-level `ratesAccess` is `granted` when rates are emitted and `denied` when they are gated out — when `denied`, do not assume the talent has no rates configured, the field is simply hidden by permission. **Rates are sensitive financial data — the widget HIDES them by default.** Even when `ratesAccess=granted` and the `rates` array is populated, the widget does NOT render the rates block in any view (compact card, table drill-down) unless `columns` explicitly includes 'rates'. The schedule tool widget never renders rates. This is a data-minimization safeguard against accidental leaks during screen-shares and casual lookups. To surface rates in the widget, set `columns: ['rates']` (or include 'rates' alongside other columns). You can still reason about rates in your text reply — but only when the user explicitly asked. **STRICT RULE for the `columns` parameter** — you MUST set it whenever the user names specific fields or uses narrowing words ('just', 'only', 'only show', 'just show', 'chỉ', 'chỉ hiển thị', 'khÃ´ng cần'). Do NOT fall back to defaults in those cases. Mapping examples:  • 'List 10 photographers and **just** show their skills' → call with arguments: { skill: 'Photographer', pageSize: 10, columns: ['skills'] }   • '5 models with their **rate info only**' → { skill: 'Model', pageSize: 5, columns: ['rates'] }   • '**Emails and phones** of all stylists' → { skill: 'Stylist', columns: ['email','phone'] }   • 'Which agency does each model belong to' → { skill: 'Model', columns: ['agencies'] }   • 'Talent based in London' → { city: 'London' }   • 'Talent in the Fashion Crew short list' → { shortListName: 'Fashion Crew' }   • 'Talent who are both Photographer AND Videographer' → { skill: 'Photographer|Videographer' }   • 'NotVerify accounts older than 30 days' → { state: 'NotVerify', createdTo: '<today-30d ISO>' }   • 'How many new talents joined in the last 3 months' → { createdFrom: '<today-3m ISO>', pageSize: 0 } (read total)   • 'List talents grouped by skill' (aggregation) → omit columns; the param has no effect on aggregation mode.   • Generic 'list/show me photographers' (no narrowing word) → omit columns; defaults to a broad set. Photo and Name are always rendered as anchors regardless of `columns`. Available column ids: jobTitle, type, employment, status, skills, agencies, email, phone, location, createdAt, pronouns, userCode, rates.

tools.description: **MANDATORY TRIGGERS** — when user prompt contains ANY of: 'available', 'availability', 'schedule', 'booking', 'confirmed', 'on hold', '1st hold', '2nd hold', 'next week', 'this week', 'on May/June/...', 'free on', 'busy on', 'OOO', 'out of office', 'unavailable on', 'inactive', 'haven't been booked', 'not booked in N days', 'access cleanup', 'dormant', 'idle freelancers' → you MUST call this tool. Do NOT respond with markdown tables, lists, or hallucinate data. The widget will render the answer visually. **Inverse query** (find talents WITHOUT bookings) → use `onlyInactive=true` paired with `dateFrom/dateTo` for the inactivity window. Common phrasings: 'freelancers not booked in 60+ days' → `onlyInactive=true, dateFrom=<60d ago>, dateTo=<today>` (chain with `query_talent_crew(employmentType=Freelancer, view=data)` first to scope pool to freelancers). **NEGATIVE TRIGGER — route to `query_planning` instead** when the prompt names a free-form production SUPPORT role like cater, catering, lunch, food, runner, driver, PA, DIT, dog handler, medic, security, prop master, set decorator, etc. These are NOT skills (skills = Photographer/Stylist/Model/Art Director/Hair&Makeup/Assistant/Videographer/DigitalProcessing). They are Custom Resource labels attached inline to planning sessions. **Do NOT pass them as `skill=...` here → the master skill catalog will not match them and the tool will return 0**. Use `query_planning(includeCustomResources=true)` instead. Query Talent & Crew scheduling data from the Resourcing Calendar — User Availability (Available/OutOfOffice/Unavailable set by the user) and Resource Bookings (1stHold/2ndHold/Confirmed/Unavailable set by manager). Use for: who is available next week, who is confirmed for a shoot date, stale holds, overbooking conflicts, per-record schedule, capacity overview. **This tool ALSO serves as a list view of talents matching the skill filter** — do NOT pre-call query_talent_crew when user prompt combines list+schedule intent (e.g. 'list all Models then their schedule next week'). Pass `skill` directly here for both the list and the schedule in ONE call. **Chain mode**: when the result is being passed as input to another tool (intermediate data extraction, NOT user-facing), set `view=data` to suppress widget render and skip avatar resolution (saves ~150ms). Default `view=widget` is correct for ALL user-facing answers. Requires dateFrom + dateTo. Scope is OPTIONAL. **Do NOT chain via query_talent_crew to pre-resolve IDs by skill.** Pass `skill` directly here — the tool resolves talents internally. When you also pass `availabilityStatus` or `bookingStatus`, the tool runs **status-first**: scans the whole studio crew pool (cap 500), filters by status, then post-filters by skill — this catches talents that a skill-first scope (cap 50) would miss. Use cases for unscoped queries: 'how many crew are unavailable on May 8?' (set pageSize=0 for count-only), 'who is Out of Office next week?'. **Name-scoped queries — mandatory chain.** When the user names a SPECIFIC talent (proper name: 'AloHa NN', 'John Photographer', 'show schedule for Tien'): FIRST call `query_talent_crew(name=..., view=data)` to resolve name → ID(s), then pass those as `talentCrewIds` here. Do NOT call this tool unscoped expecting to find the named talent in the result list — that wastes a round trip and dumps the whole crew on the user. **Session-scoped queries — chain order is mandatory.** When the user mentions a session: FIRST call `query_planning` to resolve the session — pick the right session param: `sessionCode` if user said it's a code, `sessionName` if a name, `session` if ambiguous. Then use the response's `id` (UUID) as `sessionId` here, and `timeSlots` to derive `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Do NOT call this tool first with a raw code/name — it requires a UUID. **Do NOT drop `sessionId` as a fallback** when a session-scoped query returns 0. Zero IS the answer — it means the session has no records matching the filters. Report 0 to the user (e.g. 'no 1st/2nd Hold bookings for that session — the crew are Confirmed instead'). To find out what status the session crew DO have, drop the `bookingStatus` filter while keeping `sessionId` — never the other way around. For session team composition ('who is on session X') use query_planning instead. sessionId here filters bookings linked to a specific session (1st Hold / Confirmed per shoot). Availability statuses (User Availability set by the user): Available, OutOfOffice, Unavailable. Booking statuses (Resource Booking set by manager): typically Option, Contacted, Confirmed, 1st Hold (FirstHold), 2nd Hold (SecondHold), Released, Cancelled, Unavailable — exact list depends on studio config (see _debug.cachedBookingStatusNames). Pass the canonical name (case-insensitive) — server resolves to dynamic statusId. **Multi-status filter — `bookingStatuses` / `availabilityStatuses`**: pass a JSON array of names (e.g. `bookingStatuses=["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"]`) when the intent covers multiple statuses. Records matching ANY listed status pass. Use the plural form whenever the user phrasing implies a set, not a single canonical status. **Singular vs multi → decide by user word, not by intent**. RULE: if user prompt contains an explicit canonical status word ('confirmed', '1st hold', 'first hold', '2nd hold', 'second hold', 'option', 'contacted', 'released', 'cancelled') → use SINGULAR `bookingStatus=<that word>`. Examples: 'who is **confirmed** today' → `bookingStatus=Confirmed`. 'show me **1st holds** for May 14' → `bookingStatus=FirstHold`. 'anyone **on hold** today' (vague — 1st or 2nd) → `bookingStatuses=["FirstHold","SecondHold"]`. Only use the multi-status form when the user prompt is VAGUE about status: 'who is **working/on-floor/on the books/scheduled/booked** today' → active bookings → `bookingStatuses=["Confirmed","FirstHold","SecondHold"]`. **Heuristic**: if the user typed a status word verbatim, that's the filter → singular. If they typed a generic 'working/scheduled' verb, multi. Don't mix. **Booking-vs-Availability AND-gate (LH-50337 follow-up)**: when ANY booking-status filter is set, the tool now narrows availability records to talents that survived the booking filter (and vice versa). So `bookingStatuses=[...]` will NOT leak availability-only rows for talents without a matching booking. Translation: filtering 'Confirmed today' returns only talents who actually have a Confirmed booking on that day, even though their availability records overlap. When groupBy params set, returns bucket counts instead of list. **Rendering rule**: each record carries a `deepLinkUrl`. When presenting results in text, ALWAYS wrap `displayName` as a clickable markdown link: `[displayName](deepLinkUrl)`. Never print plain names. If `displayName` is empty, fall back to talentCrewId or userCode (still wrapped). **UI rendering**: paired widget renders avatar table with status pills + inline date ranges + clickable names (Availability / Booking / On-set Role columns auto-shown when relevant data present). Per response shape:   • `hits` with ≥1 talent → widget renders compact-card / table. Text = ONE brief sentence summary PLUS optionally ONE useful insight you spot in the data (e.g. 'Found 6 confirmed photographers for May 8 — note: oanh eu has overlapping bookings May 7-15.'). Do not list each row in text — widget shows the data.   • Aggregation (`byAvailabilityStatus` / `byBookingStatus`) → widget renders bar chart. Text = ONE brief sentence summarising buckets.   • `hits` empty + `total > 0` (count-only, pageSize=0) → widget HIDES. Text MUST state the count plainly.   • `hits` empty + `total = 0` → widget HIDES. **IMPORTANT fallback**: before replying 'no one is booked', call `query_planning(dateFrom=<same>, dateTo=<same>, groupByTeamMember=true)` to check if talent are assigned on sessions without bookings. If `query_planning` returns teamMembers, present those results to the user (e.g. 'No bookings found, but these talent are assigned on sessions this week:'). Only reply 'no one is planned' if BOTH tools return empty. **Conflict API unavailability**: if `_debug.conflictApiAvailable === false`, the booking conflict service is down for this query. ALL hits will have `hasConflict=false` regardless of actual state. The widget renders a footer note, but you SHOULD also append a brief warning to your text reply (e.g. 'Note: conflict warnings are temporarily unavailable — verify holds manually'). **INACTIVE BOOKINGS — STRICT RULE**: by default the tool excludes `Cancelled` and `Released` bookings from results (active-schedule hygiene). If `_debug.inactiveCount.total > 0` in the response, the widget rendered fewer rows than exist server-side. Mention this in the text reply (e.g. 'X cancelled / Y released bookings hidden — let me know if you want to see them.'). Pass `includeInactiveBookings=true` ONLY when the user EXPLICITLY mentions cancelled, released, inactive, or 'all bookings' (e.g. 'show all bookings including cancelled', 'were any of Tien's holds released?'). Do NOT pass it for generic 'schedule for X' or 'who's available' queries. **Rates are NEVER shown via this tool.** Schedule queries are about availability and bookings, not pricing. The widget for this tool does not render rates in any view (single, list, or drill-down). If the user asks about rates after a schedule query, chain to `query_talent_crew(talentCrewIds=[<from schedule result>], columns=['rates'])` instead of re-calling the schedule tool. Do NOT write a markdown table, do NOT chain to get_talent_crew_preview, do NOT fabricate avatar URLs in text. Do NOT include deep-link URLs in text — the widget renders the name as a clickable anchor.

tools.name: update_planning_session
tools.title: Update Planning Session
tools.description: Update an existing planning session (a scheduled production shoot). **This is a write** — it changes real data. It applies a TARGETED PARTIAL update: only the fields you pass change, everything else is left untouched. **FIND THE SESSION FIRST.** This tool takes a session **id** (UUID) — it does NOT search. Use the planning-session query tool to find the session first, then pass its `id`. **FOR CREW OR TIME-SLOT EDITS, PASS THE CURRENT STATE FROM THAT SAME QUERY.** This tool never reads the session itself, so for those two field groups you must give it the current state the query returned: for `crewOps`, copy the session's `team[]` straight into `currentTeamMembers` (keep each member's `userId`, `skillId`, `sessionTeamMemberId`); for `timeSlots`, pass the COMPLETE new slot list, keeping each retained slot's `sessionTimeSlotId` from the query result. (Scalars, customProperties and customResources need NO current state — they patch in place.) **CONFIRM BEFORE CALLING — but don't be repetitive.** Two conditions must hold before you call this tool: (1) the user has seen exactly what will change — every field you're about to update, and for crew the resulting team after the ops; and (2) the user has explicitly agreed to apply it. The GOAL is an informed yes, not a fixed script. So: if you've ALREADY laid out the specific changes in the conversation (e.g. you listed the production items / fields and the user replied "yes, all of them" / "go ahead"), that satisfies both conditions — do NOT re-print the same list as a separate "preview" block and ask a second time; just call the tool. Only build an explicit preview-and-confirm step when the changes haven't been spelled out yet, or the user's request is the FIRST mention and they haven't confirmed the specifics — then show the summary and ask a direct yes/no like "Shall I apply this update?" and WAIT. Never call it on a bare first request whose specifics the user hasn't seen and approved. (After you call it, the host also shows its own Allow/Deny prompt — a second, separate gate that does not replace getting the user's informed yes.) Accepts human-readable NAMES (production type, location, workspace, producer, crew people + skills) — resolved to IDs server-side. Pass each person as the user typed them (name, email, or id) — the tool resolves it, so there's no need to look an id up first, and a failed call tells you exactly how to fix the arguments. **Writes fail hard on unresolved names**: if a person can't be matched to exactly one user, or a skill isn't a valid allowed skill the person possesses, the tool returns an error and changes nothing. **Clearing fields:** to remove the location pass `location`="No set"; to remove the producer pass `producer`=""; to reset the card color pass `color`="none"; to switch a session to editorial pass `productionType`="editorial". **crewOps** is a list of delta operations on the current team — { op:"add", person, skill? } (skill OPTIONAL — omit it or pass "none" to add the person without a skill yet), { op:"remove", person }, { op:"changeSkill", person, skill } (pass skill "none" to clear it). There's no swap — express it as remove + add. Each op fails hard if it's inconsistent with `currentTeamMembers` (add a person already on the team, remove/changeSkill a person not on it). On success it returns `{ updated, sessionId, applied, changes }`: `applied` lists which field groups were written, and **`changes` is the authoritative per-field result you should report to the user** — each field you changed appears with its new value, and a removed field shows the literal "cleared" (e.g. `changes.producer = "cleared"`). **Verify the outcome from `changes` in this response — do NOT re-query the session just to confirm a change landed** (the read model can lag a just-written change).

parameters.description: Session-card color — one of the 12 fixed colors (Google-Calendar palette). Pass the color NAME (preferred) or its numeric id 0-11. Map the user's everyday color words to the closest name using this guide: `tomato`(11) = red; `flamingo`(4) = pink / light red / coral; `tangerine`(10) = orange; `banana`(1) = yellow; `sage`(9) = light/pale green; `basil`(2) = dark green; `peacock`(8) = teal / cyan / turquoise; `blueberry`(3) = blue / dark blue; `lavender`(7) = light purple / lilac; `grape`(5) = purple / violet; `graphite`(6) = gray; `bright`(0) = white / default (no tint). E.g. "make it red" → `tomato`; "blue" → `blueberry`; "teal"/"turquoise" → `peacock`; "purple" → `grape` (or `lavender` if they say light purple). If the user names a color exactly (e.g. "tomato"), use it as-is. Pass "none"/"reset"/empty to RESET to no manual color. Sparse — omit to leave the color unchanged.

parameters.name: timeZone

Defaults to the user's timezone. **To CHANGE the session's timezone while keeping the same clock times** (e.g. 'move this shoot to Tokyo time' — 9am stays 9am, now Tokyo): set `timeZone` to the new tz, set `currentTimeZone` to the session's existing tz, and pass the session's CURRENT timeSlots back unchanged (the absolute/UTC times from the query). The tool then keeps each slot's wall-clock and recomputes it under the new tz, exactly like the app's Change-timezone action.

parameters.name: currentTimeZone
parameters.description: The session's CURRENT timezone (IANA name or tz id), copied from the planning-session query. Pass this ONLY when you're changing `timeZone` to a different value AND want the existing clock times preserved (the timezone-change case described under `timeZone`). When set, the tool reads each retained slot's wall-clock in this old timezone and re-interprets it in the new `timeZone`. Omit it if you're sending fresh slot times (bare datetimes) rather than rebasing the existing ones.

parameters.name: timeSlots
parameters.description: The COMPLETE new time-slot list (full-array replace). JSON array of { sessionTimeSlotId?, start, end }: keep each retained slot's `sessionTimeSlotId` from the query result; omit it on a new slot; drop a slot entirely to delete it. `start`/`end` are ISO datetimes carrying their own day (see create tool). **Each slot must start and end on the SAME calendar day** (in the session timezone) — a single slot CANNOT span two days, and the tool rejects one that does (e.g. 7 Jul → 8 Jul is invalid). **When the user gives a continuous range that CROSSES MIDNIGHT, you MUST SPLIT it at midnight into TWO slots — do NOT clamp the end back to the first day, and do NOT drop the after-midnight part.** Split so no requested time is lost: first slot = start → 23:59 of the start day, second slot = 00:00 of the next day → the user's end time. Example — 'from 17:00 on 7 Jul to 02:00 on 8 Jul' → [{"start":"2026-07-07T17:00","end":"2026-07-07T23:59"},{"start":"2026-07-08T00:00","end":"2026-07-08T02:00"}]. A slot needs start < end, so if the after-midnight part is zero-length (the range ends exactly at 00:00), drop the second slot and keep just [{"start":"2026-07-07T17:00","end":"2026-07-07T23:59"}]. Before sending, tell the user you've split the overnight range into two slots and confirm. **A MULTI-DAY session is likewise expressed as one slot PER DAY**: a shoot running 7–8 Jul 09:00–17:00 → TWO slots [{"start":"2026-07-07T09:00","end":"2026-07-07T17:00"},{"start":"2026-07-08T09:00","end":"2026-07-08T17:00"}], NOT one slot from 7 Jul to 8 Jul. Omit this param to leave time slots untouched.

parameters.name: crewOps
parameters.description: Delta operations on the crew. JSON array of { op, person, skill? }. op = 'add' (skill required), 'remove', or 'changeSkill' (skill required). `person` = a name, email, or userId. For **remove**, the simplest is to pass the member's `userId` from `currentTeamMembers` (it's matched directly against the team). For **add**/**changeSkill**, pass a name or email (the tool looks up the person's skills to validate the new skill). **Skill is OPTIONAL on add** — omit it or pass `skill`:"none" to put someone on the team without a skill yet. To CLEAR an existing member's skill, use changeSkill with `skill`:"none". E.g. [{"op":"add","person":"Anna","skill":"Stylist"},{"op":"add","person":"Le Ngan"},{"op":"changeSkill","person":"Carl","skill":"none"},{"op":"remove","person":"<userId>"}]. REQUIRES `currentTeamMembers`.

parameters.name: currentTeamMembers
parameters.description: The session's current crew, copied straight from the planning-session query's `team[]`. JSON array of { userId, skillId, sessionTeamMemberId }. Required whenever `crewOps` is given — the tool applies the ops to this list and sends the full result. (Booking/hold status is NOT touched by this tool — it's managed by a separate booking-status flow — so you don't need to pass it.)

parameters.name: customProperties
parameters.description: Custom properties to set (true sparse patch — only the named ones change). JSON array of { name, value }. E.g. [{"name":"Campaign","value":"Winter"}]. Values are validated against the property's type: a **Number** property needs a numeric value within ±99999999999.9999; a **Free text** property is capped at 2048 characters; a **List of options** property needs one of its defined options (case-insensitive) — a bad value returns an error listing the allowed options. Dates take ISO (e.g. '2026-06-24').

parameters.name: customResources
parameters.description: Custom resources to add/change — free-form (label, person) production-support roles (catering, driver, runner…). JSON array of { label, name }. The tool reads the session's current resources itself and overlays these by label, so pass only what changes. (Setting `name` to empty keeps the row with no person — it does NOT delete the row; to delete a row use `removeCustomResources`.)

parameters.name: removeCustomResources
parameters.description: Custom resources to DELETE — a JSON array of labels to remove entirely from the session, e.g. ["Driver","Catering"]. The tool drops these from the session's resource set and writes the rest. Use this (not an empty `name` in `customResources`) when the user wants a resource row gone.

parameters.name: productionItemOps
parameters.description: Assign / remove / move PRODUCTION ITEMS (work units) to/from this session — the assignment link only; it never changes the production item's own workflow or status. JSON array of { op, productionItemIds }, where op is 'add', 'remove', or 'move' and `productionItemIds` is an ARRAY of ids (so 'add all 12 work units of this job' is ONE op). **Get the ids from the production query tool first**, then preview which production items you'll assign and get a yes. **WHICH ID TO PASS depends on the session's content type:** for an **e-comm** (shooting-type) session, pass the work unit's `id` from query_ecomm_production. for an **editorial** session, pass the **`deliverableId`** taken from query_editorial_production's `deliverableOfFinalize.deliverableId` field. **Do NOT pass the editorial work unit's top-level `id` — editorial assignment uses the deliverableId, and a work-unit id will be rejected as non-existent.** **add vs move — choose by the production item's CURRENT state, NOT by the user's verb** (users say 'move' loosely): use **add** for a production item that isn't on any session yet (the common case); use **move** ONLY when the user names/implies the production item is currently on ANOTHER session ('from session A', 'on yesterday's shoot', 'it's on the wrong session') — move re-homes it here. When unsure, use **add**; if the backend reports an id was already on another session, the tool's warning tells you to retry that id with 'move'. Examples: 'Add the Nike hoodie work unit to this session' → add; 'Move these work units into session X' (no source named) → add; 'Move the hoodie work unit FROM session A to here' → move. **PRODUCTION-TYPE RULE (must hold for add/move):** every production item you assign MUST have the SAME production type / shooting type as the planning session's own production type. A session holds items of ONE production type only — e.g. a flat/still work unit cannot go on an on-model session, and you cannot mix two different production types in one call. Check each item's production type against the session's before assigning; if they differ, don't assign it — tell the user which items don't match instead. E.g. [{"op":"add","productionItemIds":["<id1>","<id2>"]},{"op":"move","productionItemIds":["<id3>"]}]. Best-effort: production-type-mismatched / already-assigned ids come back as a warning, the rest still apply.

tools.knownLimitations: Write tool — targeted partial update; only the fields you pass change. Id-only (find the session with query_planning first). For crew/time-slot edits pass the current state from that query (`currentTeamMembers` / `timeSlots` with their ids) — the tool never re-reads the session. Production items: `productionItemOps` assigns/removes/moves existing production items (work units) — the assignment link only, never the item's own workflow/status (get ids from query_ecomm_production; op add for an unassigned item, move only when it's on another session); production-type compatibility is enforced by the backend and rejected ids come back as a warning. Clears via a sentinel string (location "No set", producer "", color "none"). Verify from the returned `changes` map — do NOT re-query. Booking/hold status is NOT settable (separate flow, blocked by CPD-554). Requires McpWritePlanning (Access) + PlanningView (Write).
